verdict.headline: Notifications (SMS/Push/Email) all guarded with try/catch + 'silent failure with logging' contract (FcmNotificationService docblock line 19, OrderSmsNotificationBuilder.php:75-83) — V1 LOCAL ships with 0 SMS gateways seeded + 0 FCM_SERVER_KEY + empty MAIL_HOST and gracefully skips every send instead of crashing the order. Source==10 kiosk-suppression branch (C8-T1) verified intact across all three builders (OrderSmsNotificationBuilder:31, OrderMailNotificationBuilder:33, OrderPushNotificationBuilder:31) — Source enum maps APP=10 / WEB=5 / POS=15 and 'kiosk machine' orders flow through APP=10 confirmed via SimulateKioskOrders.php:49 + E2ESoakCommand.php:992. Payment gateways: 3 PG rows seeded (FIX-1 verified — Cash On Delivery + Credit + Stripe), Stripe constructor instantiates without TypeError, Stripe row carries placeholder credentials and status=10 (DISABLED) so V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne stays cash-only as designed. Stripe::handleWebhook + Senangpay::webhook both signature-verify, both idempotent via WebhookEvent::firstOrCreate + DB UNIQUE(provider, webhook_id), both throttled 60/min, both VerifyCsrfToken-excluded, both LIVE-probed returning 500 misconfigured (Stripe — STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET not set in dev .env; SenangPay — gateway not enabled in payment_gateways) which is the correct NF525-conservative behaviour. IdempotencyKeyMiddleware (FROZEN §7) frozen-zone diff = 0 (md5 06644cd1e923d0863947c2ad4d37d2c5, 244 lines, single creation commit 7f8c771d8, no subsequent edit). K2-HEAL-05 DrainStrandedCpnCommand registered every-5-min Paris with onOneServer + withoutOverlapping + runInBackground (Kernel:198-206); commands sentinel 11/11 PASS; observed one real stranded CPN (order #1 / token=txn_debug_1 / 4505 min old) that the cron correctly tried to drain but ValidationException-failed because Stripe is not in payment.pilot_restrict.allowed_methods (BY DESIGN per command docblock lines 67-74 — 'a stranded CPN in a Stripe-disabled environment is a real fault that SHOULD page ops rather than be silently absorbed'). The audit_logs row #98 'payment.method_restricted' proves the pilot lock activated AND was NF525-chained. 38 webhook + payment sentinels PASS in this run. 3 documented findings — none ship-blocking.

A_H10_01_unsigned_stripe_webhook_replay.scenario: Capture a legitimate Stripe webhook (charge.succeeded for €1000 order), wait 1 day, replay against a different victim order.
A_H10_01_unsigned_stripe_webhook_replay.defense_1: Stripe-Signature is HMAC-SHA-256 over (timestamp.payload, signing_secret). Modified payload → signature mismatch → constructEvent throws SignatureVerificationException → HTTP 400.
A_H10_01_unsigned_stripe_webhook_replay.defense_2: Even with a correctly-signed legit replay (same payload), the 300s replay-tolerance check rejects events >300s old → HTTP 400. F-3 SYNC P1 V1.0.1 quick win.
A_H10_01_unsigned_stripe_webhook_replay.defense_3: If somehow 1+2 pass, WebhookEvent::firstOrCreate keys on event.id → second receipt returns 200 'duplicate_ignored', NO second CapturePaymentNotification created.
A_H10_01_unsigned_stripe_webhook_replay.verdict: TRIPLE DEFENDED — signature + 300s replay window + DB UNIQUE event_id

A_H10_02_senangpay_hmac_timing_oracle.scenario: Attacker submits 10,000 webhook attempts with varied hash values, measures response time to deduce expected HMAC byte-by-byte.
A_H10_02_senangpay_hmac_timing_oracle.defense: Senangpay.php:110  hash_equals($expectedHash, $hash) — constant-time comparison resistant to timing-side-channel. PHP's hash_equals is the recommended way (vs ===) precisely for this.
A_H10_02_senangpay_hmac_timing_oracle.amplifier_defense: throttle:60,1 — 60 invalid attempts per minute is far below the millions needed to extract a 64-hex-char HMAC.

A_H10_03_idempotency_replay_attack.scenario: Attacker captures X-Idempotency-Key from a legit POST /api/admin/cash-drawer/open with €500, replays with €5000 payload + same key.
A_H10_03_idempotency_replay_attack.defense: IdempotencyKeyMiddleware computes payload-hash on first POST + stores under (branch_id, user_id, hash(key)). Same key + different payload → HTTP 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT + Idempotency-Key-Conflict header. Original cached response (€500) is NOT returned.

A_H10_04_pilot_bypass_via_artisan.scenario: Operator with shell access runs `php artisan stripe:drain-stranded-cpn` while Stripe is not pilot-allowlisted — does the bypass-via-CLI side-step the pilot guard?
A_H10_04_pilot_bypass_via_artisan.actual_outcome: Observed live — payment.method_restricted ValidationException thrown by PaymentService::payment(), command logs 'failed: 1', audit_logs row #98 'payment.method_restricted' written. The pilot gate is enforced at the PaymentService layer (NOT at the route/controller layer), so CLI/HTTP/webhook all bottleneck through the same gate. Defense in depth.
A_H10_04_pilot_bypass_via_artisan.verdict: DEFENDED — pilot enforcement at service layer, not gate-bypassable via artisan

A_H10_05_stripe_metadata_order_id_spoofi.scenario: Attacker crafts a fake charge.succeeded webhook (with valid signature — assumes leaked webhook secret) carrying metadata.order_id=victim_order_id to mark victim's order PAID without paying.
A_H10_05_stripe_metadata_order_id_spoofi.defense_1: Leaked webhook secret would be the root cause — refuses-to-boot guard at AppServiceProvider:331-341 prevents accidental empty deploy, and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is V1.0.X cloud-prep (not on V1 LOCAL config).
A_H10_05_stripe_metadata_order_id_spoofi.defense_2: Even with a valid signature, the corresponding CapturePaymentNotification row carries the FAKE charge's balance_transaction token. When the legitimate customer's browser visits /payment.success (or the drain cron picks up), PaymentService::payment validates the order's currently-bound stripe charge token via Stripe API call → mismatch → ValidationException.
A_H10_05_stripe_metadata_order_id_spoofi.defense_3: Stripe::handleWebhook does NOT mutate order.payment_status directly — it writes a CPN row + bridges via Stripe::success / drain cron. The order flip path is gated by /payment.success → Stripe::success → PaymentService::payment which double-checks via Stripe API call. Pure-DB-replay does not transit Stripe API, so the FAKE charge token would not match an actual Stripe charge.
A_H10_05_stripe_metadata_order_id_spoofi.verdict: DEFENDED (multi-layer) — requires both leaked-secret AND Stripe API call to succeed for a complete pwn. V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne with Stripe DISABLED has no live secret to leak.

p2_p3_documented_caveats.title: Source enum naming-comment drift (kiosk vs APP)
p2_p3_documented_caveats.details: Source enum (app/Enums/Source.php) defines const APP=10 / WEB=5 / POS=15. Comment in OrderSms/Mail/PushNotificationBuilder.php:31/33/31 says 'Source 10 = Kiosk Machine'. three_critical_findings.title: FCM dual-path inconsistency — LEGACY endpoint+key auth in order-event lane vs FCM HTTP v1+OAuth2 in admin-broadcast lane
three_critical_findings.scope: app/Services/FcmNotificationService.php (used by SendFcmNotificationJob → order-event listeners SendFcmOnOrderCreated + SendFcmOnOrderStatusChange)  vs  app/Services/FirebaseService.php (used by PushNotificationService → admin broadcast fan-out)
three_critical_findings.why_it_matters: Google has formally deprecated FCM legacy server-key auth. Order-event lane will break when Google sunsets, while admin-broadcast lane will continue working. Visible asymmetric outage during a routine credential refresh would surface as 'kitchen FCM works in admin push but not in real-time order creation' — confusing on-call diagnosis.
three_critical_findings.current_v1_impact: ZERO — V1 LOCAL has FCM_SERVER_KEY=NULL so both paths early-return with Log::warning('skipping notification') without firing any HTTP request.
three_critical_findings.remediation: (a) Move SendFcmNotificationJob to call FirebaseService::sendNotification (single source of truth). (b) Delete FcmNotificationService class or convert it into a thin wrapper around FirebaseService. (c) Add tests/Feature/Sentinels/FcmTransportConsistencySentinelTest asserting both lanes go through the same HTTP endpoint constant.

three_critical_findings.title: Stranded CPN drain pilot-gate behaviour is correct but observability could surface the pre-activation noise to OPS
three_critical_findings.scope: app/Console/Commands/Stripe/DrainStrandedCpnCommand.php every-5-min cron writes audit_logs 'payment.method_restricted' + fiscal log 'stripe.drain_cpn.failed' for every stranded CPN row that exists while Stripe is not in the pilot allowlist.
three_critical_findings.why_it_matters: On a healthy V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne (cash-only pilot, no real Stripe traffic), there should be ZERO CPN rows ever. The current dev DB has 1 residue row from 2026-05-24 that will continue generating an audit_logs entry + fiscal log entry every 5 min when production schedule:run is enabled. If OPS doesn't clean up dev-stranded residue before going live, the audit_logs chain accumulates noise at 288 rows/day (12/hour × 24h). Not corruption, just clutter that obscures real anomalies.
three_critical_findings.current_v1_impact: ZERO if dev hygiene is done before go-live (single SQL DELETE), or LOW-LOW if not cleaned (audit_logs grows by ~288 inert rows/day until cleared).
three_critical_findings.remediation: (a) Pre-cutover runbook step: DB::table('capture_payment_notifications')->where('token','txn_debug_1')->delete();  (b) Add a guard in DrainStrandedCpnCommand: if PaymentService::assertMethodAllowed throws AND CPN age > 1 day, write the audit_logs entry ONCE per (order_id, day) instead of per-run (rate-limit the noise). V1.0.X backlog.
